content.title: Extraordinary Visitor, Ordinary Day | Mundane Tasks Normalize the Premise
content.summary: Introduce one original extraordinary visitor at an ordinary threshold, preserve the same identity through at least four non-repeating mundane tasks with visible results and normal social responses, then shift once to dusk and return to the opening boundary for a restrained acknowledgment.

quick_start.input_format: original extraordinary visitor and ordinary threshold + stable identity anchors + at least four non-repeating mundane tasks + familiar tool, complete action and visible result per task + normal world response + one day-to-night shift + return to the opening boundary
quick_start.recommended_input: A translucent municipal automaton arrives at a coastal apartment lobby, rides a cargo tricycle, collects a library parcel, repairs a wind vane, sorts communal mail, waters a roof planter and returns to the same lobby charging niche at dusk.
required_anchors: Establish one original extraordinary visitor at an ordinary threshold before the route begins.
Keep the same identity anchors across at least four non-repeating mundane tasks.
Let the world respond normally and avoid explaining the visitor's origin.
Use one day-to-night transition and return to the opening boundary with a restrained acknowledgment.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Introduce one original extraordinary visitor at an ordinary threshold, preserve the same identity through at least four non-repeating mundane tasks with visible results and normal social responses, then shift once to dusk and return to the opening boundary for a restrained acknowledgment.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Open on one unmistakably extraordinary but original visitor at a familiar domestic threshold. Preserve the same identity anchors across a one-way daytime route of at least four visually different mundane responsibilities. Each chapter must contain one familiar tool or exchange, one complete action and one visible result; surrounding people and environments respond normally rather than explaining the visitor. Use object or hand-state handoffs to keep the montage causal, then change the time of day once and return the visitor to the opening boundary for a restrained final acknowledgment. The reusable mechanism is extraordinary identity normalized by cumulative ordinary competence and a same-place day return—not the source alien design, suburban house, car, service window, drink, grill, manicure, garden, clothing, exact tasks, camera positions, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish one original extraordinary visitor at an ordinary threshold before the route begins.
invariants.purpose: Creates an immediate contrast question without requiring exposition.
invariants.ablation_failure: A conventional subject removes the normalization tension; a random location removes the social baseline.

invariants.rule: Keep the same identity anchors across at least four non-repeating mundane tasks.
invariants.purpose: Turns the premise into a coherent day rather than a novelty reel.
invariants.ablation_failure: Identity drift or repeated duties break cumulative familiarity.

invariants.rule: Give every task one familiar tool or exchange, a complete action and a visible result.
invariants.purpose: Lets the audience understand competence without narration.
invariants.ablation_failure: Poses or incomplete motions leave only costume spectacle.

invariants.rule: Let the world respond normally and avoid explaining the visitor's origin.
invariants.purpose: Normalization is produced through behavior and social acceptance.
invariants.ablation_failure: Exposition or panic changes the mechanism into lore or threat.

invariants.rule: Use one day-to-night transition and return to the opening boundary with a restrained acknowledgment.
invariants.purpose: Converts multiple errands into a bounded daily loop.
invariants.ablation_failure: A random final location leaves the route episodic and unresolved.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source gray alien head, eyes, body proportions, shirt, hands and exact greeting performance
the source suburban porch, car interior, road, drive-through window, drink and payment exchange
the source grill, meat, manicure interaction, garden hose, plants and residential night background
the source shot order, lenses, framing, lighting progression, exact 30-second rhythm and transitions
the source creator identity, platform overlay, watermark, model claim and branding
